name: Pike push-up
summary: Hips high in an inverted V, lower the head toward the floor between the hands and press up.
setup: Hands and feet on the floor, hips pushed high so the body makes an upside-down V, side-on to the phone at floor level. Bend the elbows to lower the top of the head toward the floor, then press back up.
brief: Hands and feet on the floor, hips pushed high so the body makes an upside-down V. Bend the elbows to lower the top of the head toward the floor, then press back up.
why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted.
contraindications: Shoulder or wrist pain; high blood pressure when the head is low.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Head landing on the floor
faults.tip: The head goes down between the hands, and never takes weight.

faults.label: Hips dropping
faults.tip: Keep the hips stacked over the shoulders so the press is vertical.

faults.label: Hips dropping out of the pike
faults.tip: As the hips drop it becomes a normal push-up and the shoulders stop working.

faults.label: Cutting depth
faults.tip: Lower until the head nearly touches.

guide.stop: Shoulder or wrist pain, or dizziness.

points.t: Bend to lower the head; press to straight.
